messages:
jen-m: Quick ask — we need a refreshed battlecard for the webinar next Thursday and a one-pager for SDRs. Scope: cloud AI platforms vs LLM API players vs infra vendors. Focus on field-ready hooks, a short benchmark narrative, and 3 rebuttals per competitor. Can someone draft a version today?

tyler-k: I can draft the cloud vs. redwood section. Thinking: latency SLAs, transparent unit economics, and rollout controls as our differentiators.

maria-g: +1 on SLAs. Also call out Dedicated & Private as primary rebuttals vs cloud-managed endpoints — customers care about predictable throughput.

aj: For infra vendors (self-hosted runtimes) we should emphasize the platform + ops cost delta and our routing/fallback story. Field line: “You get control without building the stack.”

emily-s: For LLM API players, quick punchlines: model access vs serving controls, and quality/regression guardrails (evals). SDR-friendly hook: “Same API today across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private — ship once, deploy anywhere.”

dave-p: Can we include a short benchmark narrative? One-paragraph that sales can read out: example comparing p95 latency and effective $/1k tokens across typical request shapes.

maria-g: Draft bench snapshot to use in narrative:
```
workload: chat (avg 256 tokens, dynamic prefixes)
redwood-hosted (redwood-1.2): p95=220ms, eff cost= $0.60/1k tokens
cloud-managed: p95=480ms, eff cost= $1.10/1k tokens
self-hosted infra: p95=260ms (cold starts), eff cost variable (ops + infra)
```

aj: Love it. Add callouts: prefix/KV cache and autoscaling matter most for chat. Those are our levers — mention intelligent batching and caching in 1-liner.

jen-m: For rebuttals, let's keep them one-liners. Example sets: 
- Cloud AI platforms: "They hide variability behind managed endpoints — but you trade off predictable unit economics and deployment control."
- LLM API players: "Wide model selection, but few tools for rollouts, regressions, or private deployments at scale."
- Infra vendors: "You get flexibility but must invest in ops; we provide the runtime + orchestration so teams don't become infra shops."

emily-s: Can marketing craft a quick cheat-sheet: 3 bullets per competitor, one-sentence customer example, and suggested rebuttal question for AE (e.g., 'How do you handle model regressions in prod?'). I can draft copy.

sam-bot: Reminder: upcoming webinar registrants list will be available by EOD — link: https://events.redwood.ai/webinar-registrants (use for targeted outreach).

maria-g: Also add a short FAQ on security: highlight Private (VPC/on-prem) and KMS/HSM options vs cloud native encryption claims. That helps enterprise reps.

dave-p: I'll assemble everything into a 1-pager + a 2-slide battlecard carousel. ETA end of day. Need final sign-off from product on the benchmark numbers.

tyler-k: Tagging @product-review once Dave posts. If product flags numbers, we'll swap to relative language (">2x cost at p95 under certain workloads") to avoid absolute claims.

jen-m: Perfect. Emily, can you own the SDR cheat-sheet? Maria + Dave, collate bench sources. Tyler + AJ: finalize competitor one-liners. I'll review before 6pm. Thanks all :rocket:
